name: MegaUSD
oneLiner: MegaETH's dollar stablecoin is issued through Ethena's stack and backed by an undisclosed mix of USDC and USDtb; USDtb primarily invests in BUIDL.
collateral: USDC and USDtb in undisclosed current proportions; USDtb's upstream reserves primarily use BlackRock BUIDL via Securitize alongside liquid stablecoins.
pegMechanism: Issued on Ethena's USDtb rails; reserve yield funds MegaETH sequencer costs

mechanismArchetypeReview.reviewer: SONG-2 Safety Score V9 mechanism review
mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: MegaETH and Ethena sources establish that USDm is issued through USDtb rails and that USDtb uses tokenized Treasury exposure with a stablecoin redemption reserve. They do not provide a measured USDm composition or the current compiler-required duration, liquidity, custody, valuation, seniority, and loss-recovery facts for the inherited mechanism, so the review remains bounded rather than inferred.

dependencyReview.rationale: MegaUSD's transparency API now publishes dated per-custodian backing amounts; at 2026-09-29T14:53:11Z it showed USDC $17,439,383.81 (99.8803%) and USDtb $20,915.84 (0.1197%) against $17,460,299.65 total backing, which the megausd-custody live adapter publishes as the 99.9/0.1 collateral mix. The reviewed relationships enumerate both collateral exposures exactly as mapped to the live reserve slices. MegaETH's 2025-09-08 launch blog documents USDm v1 as issued on Ethena's USDtb rails, so the USDtb relationship additionally carries the control-operator role for that v1 issuance stack; the claim is historical rather than a present-tense rail — the same blog states the architecture lets the reserve composition change over time, Ethena's whitelabel page (retrieved 2026-09-29) lists USDM as 'backed by USDtb & USDC on launch' under dynamic backing allocation, and the 2026-09-29 transparency snapshot above shows the allocation is now ≈99.9% USDC with USDtb a residual backing asset, while on-chain the USDm mint authority is an owner-managed addMinter/removeMinter whitelist whose active mint path (latest mint 2026-09-28) runs through unlabeled contracts, so no current source confirms USDtb rails as today's operative mint/redeem path. The registry authors dependencies as a single weight budget capped at 1, so a full-basket asset records that role on the USDtb collateral anchor (whose weight is the basket share) rather than as a separate full-weight mechanism entry, following the multi-role encoding used for usdf-astherus; the single ≤1 authoring budget cannot express a full-weight control operator on a 0.1% collateral anchor — a methodology gap flagged for the owner. Role edges are scored on cards and are not part of the serial/basket map projection. The approximately 90% BUIDL allocation cited at launch is USDtb's target reserve mix, not a measured USDm composition.

relationships.reason: USDC backing leg held across the five named MegaUSD custodian addresses; live adapter weight 99.9% from the issuer transparency API.
USDtb backing leg held across the same custodian set; live adapter weight 0.1% from the issuer transparency API.

USDm v1 was issued on Ethena's USDtb rails at launch (MegaETH blog, 2025-09-08), recording Ethena as the upstream control operator for that v1 issuance stack; current issuer-side sources (retrieved 2026-09-29) still present USDm as Ethena-powered, but with dynamically allocated backing now ≈99.9% USDC / ≈0.1% USDtb, and no current source confirms USDtb rails as today's operative mint/redeem path. The weight carries the anchor's basket share under the registry's single dependency weight budget.
